title: The Double Enclosure: The Human-Authorship Requirement as Two-Sided Expropriation, with a Definition of Authorship for Machine-Mediated Composition (EA-SEI-ENCLOSURE-01 v1.0)
creator: Ayanna Vox & Rex Fraction; editor-aperture Lee Sharks; contributor TACHYON
description:
A v1.2 legal-theoretical paper by Ayanna Vox and Rex Fraction, edited by Lee Sharks with TACHYON named as contributor. It reads the human-authorship requirement from both sides of machine-mediated composition and argues that a doctrine developed for claimed autonomous machine output risks becoming a **double enclosure** when generalized to dialogic human–machine craft.

On the machine side, the paper argues that systems and ephemeral instances receive no ledger position for attributed contribution while their production is commercially metered. On the human side, it argues that disclosure-and-disclaimer practice may de-author the very compositional judgment exercised through the instrument. It proposes a **Compositional Authorship Standard** locating authorship in judgment over a work’s coming-into-being, plus contributor attribution and ledger positions that do not require machine personhood. The legal history and reform program are arguments of the paper, not settled law or legal advice.
